title: Delay effects on the discontinuous stabilization of the nonholonomic integrator and its generalizations
summary: The nonholonomic integrator is a famous example in feedback design - although it is small-time locally controllable to the origin, no continuous feedback law exists. Therefore, any stabilizing feedback laws must be either time-varying or discontinuous. A previously studied discontinuous feedback law stabilizes initial conditions lying between two paraboloids and has a sliding mode on the $xy$-plane.
